text:
Eighteen games in, the Flyers have 12 points, a 4-10-4 record and a 2% chance of making the playoffs by our simulations. The losses are not flukes. Philadelphia has taken 41% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count), and only the goaltending has kept the goal column from looking worse: 60 allowed against 63.5 expected.

The one bright light is also the loudest subplot. Matvei Michkov has 11 points in his last 10 games against 7.4 expected, and his line with Noah Cates and Porter Martone has won 61% of the expected goals in its 78 minutes together. Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports wrote that "the kid is the leading goal scorer on the team" and that if there is tension in the room around him, "the group has to come together & fix it." We can't see inside the room. We can see that Michkov's line is the only one tilting the ice.

The rest is a scoring problem on top of a chance problem: 39 goals from 47.4 expected. Some of that should turn. A 4.17 penalties-a-game habit won't help it turn faster.

What to watch: a road trip O'Connor called important "in the grand scheme of the season." In mid-November, that is rarely a good sign.
headline: The kid is the story, for better and worse
